title: AI imaging measures change during cardiac amyloidosis treatment
summary: Automated cardiac segmentation quantified serial SPECT/CT scans in 45 patients receiving transthyretin amyloidosis therapies. Several tracer-uptake markers decreased after treatment, and selected changes were associated with functional measures. These exploratory observational results do not prove treatment causality or removal of amyloid deposits; affected-volume measures did not significantly decline.
organization: Medical University of Vienna; University Hospital Essen

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Serial baseline/follow-up clinical imaging, automated cardiac-region quantification and exploratory associations with functional measurements.
evidence.unknown: Controlled treatment effects, cross-scanner generalizability and clinical decision benefit remain unestablished; the paper has inconsistent aggregate marker counts and small treatment subgroups.
evidence.ai_role: A pretrained anatomical segmentation network maps cardiac structures to SPECT, enabling standardized regional tracer measurements over time.
